title: 1901, May taken upon completion by Charles McCormack
description: Charles A. McCormack held the dual roles of President and Superintendent of Construction for the Hartland Bridge Company. Born around 1841 to William McCormack and Eunice DeGrasse, Charles spent much of his youth with his uncle, Edward DeGrasse. Although his formal education ended at fourteen, he became skilled in trapping, lumbering, and carpentry, eventually establishing himself as a successful farmer. Among his many accomplishments were the construction of several highway bridges—including the Aker Creek Bridge at Lower Brighton—and the design of Hartland’s first water system. On May 30, 1901, Charles experienced a rare moment of professional pride: as superintendent, he wrote a long-anticipated letter to himself, in his capacity as President, confirming the bridge’s completion. He then forwarded this letter to the provincial government, officially marking the successful end of a truly remarkable project.
